item.description: Helene Kröller-Müller assembled the world’s second-largest collection of van Gogh paintings. Now, for the first time in decades, they are on show together in a Dutch forest.
item.dc:creator: Nina Siegal

item.title: The Lucas Museum’s Architect Wants to Help You Escape From Reality
item.description: Ma Yansong, China’s reigning starchitect, lets his buildings wrapped in nature do the shouting.
item.dc:creator: Sam Lubell
item.media:credit: Sela Shiloni for The New York Times

item.title: Museum Regrets Renting Space to 9/11 Event That Aired Conspiracy Theories
item.description: As New York commemorated the 25th anniversary of the attacks, El Museo del Barrio rented space to a group skeptical of the explanation of what caused the twin towers to come down.
item.dc:creator: Colin Moynihan
item.media:credit: Vincent Tullo for The New York Times
item.media:description: El Museo del Barrio, a Manhattan museum of Latin Art that operates out of a city-owned building, rented space for a conference on 9/11 where speakers said they felt the real story of the attacks has been covered up.

item.title: Adam Pendleton Is Painting the White Cube Black
item.description: On Oct. 10, the artist’s exhibition, “Some Wild Kind of Language,” opens at the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam. It will upend expectations.
item.dc:creator: Nina Siegal
item.media:credit: Clifford Prince King for The New York Times
item.media:description: Adam Pendleton with his painting “The Door (A Days Painting),” 2026, which will be at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam.

item.title: The Alejandro Mario Yllanes Paintings Saved From a Dumpster
item.description: Alejandro Mario Yllanes, a self-taught Bolivian painter, made searingly political works championed by Diego Rivera. Their journey to major museums is a 50-year saga full of mysteries.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Burnett
item.media:credit: Nic Antaya for The New York Times
item.media:description: “Lake Titicaca” by Alejandro Mario Yllanes will hang at the Toledo Museum of Art in Ohio. The painting was one of about a dozen found in a dumpster around 1978.

item.title: He Asked ‘Why Such a Nice Girl Would Paint Such Wild Pictures.’ The Rest Is Art History.
item.description: Gallerists have uncovered rare works by Marguerite and William Zorach, shining light on the pioneering collaborators. Their modern art love story bows at the Independent 20th Century fair.
item.dc:creator: Hilarie M. Sheets

item.title: New Bid to Claim Cranach Paintings Held by Norton Simon Museum

item.title: Two Centuries On, Smithsonian Connects Jefferson’s Hair to Hemings’s Children
